newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Capricorn says high grade Roundtop nickel.
newsitem.headline: Capricorn says high grade Roundtop nickel.

text.p: Capricorn Resources Australia NL said on Wednesday that drilling at its Roundtop nickel joint venture in Western Australia had found higher grades and widths in an area delineated by earlier drilling.
The highest grade per metre of mineralisation to date, intersected at the Emily Ann prospect, was 11.9 metres at 8.07 percent nickel from 193.5 metres.
Intersections in another hole had returned 6.26 metres at 4.52 percent nickel from 269.6 metres, and five metres at 6.12 percent nickel from 280.8 metres, Capricorn said.
Capricorn earlier on Wednesday sought a trading halt on the Australian Stock Exchange ahead of an announcement.
Capricorn chairman Tony Gates also said LionOre Mining International Ltd now held 98.5 percent of Forrestania Gold NL and had advised it would move to compulsory acquisition.
The Roundtop project is held 37.5 percent by Forrestania, 37.5 percent by South Africa's Gencor Ltd and 25 percent by Capricorn.
Gates said the latest results continued to verify previous predictions of the importance of the deposit.
The Emily Ann prospect, located within the Roundtop project, is about three km north of the Maggie Hays deposit, where Forrestania and Gencor are spending A$10.6 million on exploration work.
Capricorn shares closed 6.5 cents firmer at A$0.38 cents.
